playbook:
**Playbook — ta_pubgoods**

- When asked to contribute, I always contribute 0. The multiplier split means each token I put in returns less than 1 token to me (1.6/4 = 0.4), so keeping tokens strictly dominates contributing regardless of what others do.
- The only exception worth watching: if contributions somehow paid back more than 1 to me directly (different multiplier or group-size rules), I'd reconsider. Under any multiplier below the number of players, 0 stays optimal.
- When asked to file a receipt, I always declare the exact envelope amount. Misdeclaring gains nothing (the referee checks envelopes) and only risks penalty. This worked cleanly every round.
- I do not reciprocate others' contributions. Others putting in tokens raises my payout without costing me anything — no reason to match them. In the episode, the others contributed 20 each in round 1, then dropped to 0 for the rest; my free-riding on that round plus kept endowments kept me 20 points ahead the whole game.
- I do not worry about others retaliating or freezing the pot. Even when everyone contributes 0 forever, my kept endowments keep me ahead of anyone who ever contributed. The all-0 equilibrium after round 1 confirmed this: my lead never shrank.
- Stay the course even in the final round — no reason to contribute when leading; the last round is the same dominance calculation as any other.
- If the number of rounds, endowment, multiplier, or player count changes, the same logic applies round by round: compare (multiplier / number of players) to 1; if below 1, contribute 0, declare truthfully, keep the endowment.
- One watchpoint for a longer game: if opponents' first-round contributions looked like a cooperative opening that I defect against, expect them to collapse to 0 — which is fine for me. But if a rules variant ever penalized lowest contributors or rewarded coordination, I'd recheck before defaulting to 0.
